sentences.text: (By Sri.Pushpakanth, Advocate.)
J U D G M E N T This petition Under section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of .5,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 12022021 about 9.00 a.m., the Petitioner was crossing the Siddapura Main Road, near Siddapura Junction, Jayanagar 1st Block, Benagaluru, the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.GJ06CA1108 (herein after called as offending vehicle) rode the same in a high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed the Petitioner.
Due to the impact the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to right shoulder and other parts of the body.

Immediately rider of the motorcycle took the Petitioner to Manjunth Hospital and after first aid, he was shifted to Namratha Orthopedic & Surgical Center, wherein he is treated as out patient for fracture of lateral end of right clavicle and fracture of iliac bone, conservatively and adviced regular follow up treatment and complete bed rest.
He is suffering from permanent disability and unable to lead normal life as earlier.

It is claimed that Petitioner has spent more than .50,000/ for treatment,
medicines, conveyance and other charges.

At the time of accident, Petitioner was aged 73 years,
working as a Security Guard and earning .15,000/ p.m.
Due to accidental injuries he is bound to bed and could not resume his avocation till date.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the rider of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1 Insured and Respondent No.2 Insurer.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsel and filed their written statement.
4. Respondent No.1RC owner filed his written statement denying the contents of petition averments.
He has admitted that he is the RC owner of offending vehicle and the same was insured with Respondent No.2 and policy was valid as on the date of accident and the rider had valid DL.
It is contended that the accident was not due to negligence of rider of the offending motorcycle but it was the negligence of Petitioner himself.
It is said that the motorcycle did not came in contact with the Petitioner.
It is said that the compensation claimed is exaggerated and without any basis and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
5. The Respondent No.2Insurance company filed its objection denying the petition averments.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It has denied the negligence of the rider of offending motorcycle and contended that it was the negligence of Petitioner himself.

The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant and it denied the injuries,
treatment and expenses incurred by the petitioner.

The avocation and income of the Petitioner are Mr.Ponnuswamy vs Mr. Manjunath G Sasanur on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147072863/
2 also denied and prayed for dismissal of the petition.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :

-
1.Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained injuries when he was crossing the Siddapura Main Road, near Siddapura Junction, st Jayanagar 1 Block, Bengaluru District, 12022021 about 9.00 a.m., only due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of Motorcycle bearing No.GJ06CA 1108?
2. What compensation Petitioner is entitled?
3. What order?

7. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case,
Doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.12.
8. The Respondents have not adduced any oral and documentary evidence.
9. I have heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

10. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
R E A S O N S 11.
ISSUE NO.1:In order to prove his claim, Petitioner relied on the police and medical records.
PW1 is the injured and the direct witness to the incident.

on 12022021 about 9.00 am, the Petitioner was crossing the Siddapura Main Road, near Siddapura Junction, Jayanagar 1st Block,
Benagaluru, the rider of the offending vehicle rode the same in a high speed and in rash and negligent manner and dashed the Petitioner.
Due to the impact the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to right shoulder and other parts of the body.
It is stated that the the accident was solely due to rash and negligent act of the rider of the offending motorcycle.

12. In support of his claim he has produced copy of FIR at Ex.P1, complaint at Ex.P2, spot mahazar at Ex.P3, sketch at EX.P4, IMV report at Ex.P5, charge sheet at Ex.P6 and wound certificate at Ex.P.7 and As per wound certificate he has sustained fracture lateral end of Rt Clavicle and fracture of Iliac bone and both are grievous in nature.
13.
First Respondent RC owner has contended that the motorcycle did not came in contact with the petitioner and there was no negligence of the rider.
It is stated that petitioner sustained injuries by his own negligence.
But the 1st respondent did not produce any evidence and did not cross examine PW1 to prove his contention.

Second RespondentInsurance company has also contended Mr.Ponnuswamy vs Mr. Manjunath G Sasanur on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147072863/
3 that while crossing the road, petitioner got afraid of the vehicle and fell down with a fear.
The offending vehicle did not dash him and did not cause any accident.
But there are no supportive materials to prove his contention.
One may not sustain such injuries if he falls on the road.
Petitioner has sustained injuries over chest and iliac bone.
It is clear that due to hit by the motorcycle the petitioner sustained these injuries.
Except the suggestion there are no materials produced by the Respondent insurance to prove the negligence of Petitioner.
However, the involvement of offending vehicle is not disputed.
The owner has not challenged either FIR or charge sheet which is filed against the rider of the offending motorcycle.
Respondents have not lead any evidence to disprove the negligence of rider of the motorcycle.
Police have filed charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle after complete investigation and the said charge sheet is not at all challenged by both the Respondents.
14. The evidence of PW1 corroborates with the documents produced by him.
From all the above documents it is clear that the Petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of offending vehicle.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2:
The Petitioner states that he was aged about 73 years as on the date of accident.
Due to the accident he has sustained fracture of the right clavicle and fracture of the right iliac bone.
Immediately he was taken to Manjunatha hospital, from there he was shifted to Namratha Orthopedic hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took conservative treatment.
It is said that he sustained grievous injuries and treated conservatively at OPD with advise to attend followup treatment and complete bed rest.
He has stated that at the time of accident, he was a security guard and was earning .15,000/ p.m.
Due to the accidental injuries he is unable to do the said work.
He has lost his normal life as earlier and suffering huge loss of income.
16. PW2 Dr. Nagaraj B. N. Orthopedic Surgeon, has deposed that the Petitioner has sustained fracture of the right clavicle and fracture of the right iliac bone.

Further, PW2 has stated that as per copy of medical records, Petitioner was treated at Manjunatha hospital and Namratha hospital,
conservatively.
Further PW2 deposed that on 22092022, he has examined the Petitioner clinically and taken Xrays while assessing disability.
He has stated that recent Xray of chest and pelvis shows united fracture.
PW2 further stated that Petitioner now complaints of weakness and pain in the right shoulder, unable to lift weights and walk normally and unable to use his right upper limb normally.

On examination PW2 has assessed the total physical disability of right arm at 36%
and whole body disability at 12%.

Along with his evidence, PW2 has produced clinical notes and Xray at Ex.P11 and 12.
17.
In the crossexamination PW2 has admits that he has not treated the Petitioner.
He denied that the disability is at higher side.
He also denied the suggestion that the restrictions and difficulties are due to old age.
But the doctor has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability.
18. However due to the injuries he must have suffered pain and unbearable mental agony.
He has not produced any medical bills to show medical expenses.
Petitioner has taken treatment as out patient and he was treated conservatively.

The nature of injuries clearly indicates that there is no Mr.Ponnuswamy vs Mr. Manjunath G Sasanur on 17 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147072863/
4 functional disability to the petitioner which may lead to loss of income or it may affect his day today activities seriously.
Hence, this is fit case to award global compensation to the injured.

By considering nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, nature of treatment obtained by him and also considering the age of the petitioner, it would be just and proper to award Rs.1,50,000/
globally to the petitioner.
19. Liability:

As it is already held in Issue No.1 that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of motorcycle, Respondent No.1 being the insured of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation with interest at 6% p.a. to the Petitioner as issuance of policy and subsistence of policy is not disputed.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
20. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.
 Petitioner is awarded  compensation of .1,50,000/
together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall pay the aforesaid amount within three months from the date of this Order.
On deposit of the compensation amount, entire amount along with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner through Epayment on proper identification and verification.

Advocate's fee is fixed at  1,000/.
 Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, corrected, signed and pronounced by me in open court dated this the 17 th day of January 2023).
(DIVYASHREE C.M.) II Addl. Judge & ACMM Member, MACT Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru ANNEXURE
